item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00360","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C08","C15","C12"],"selected_candidate_label":"C08","confidence":0.98,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C08 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template: both directives use the same compact operative structure declaring specified tax returns open to inspection by a named body and making inspection subject to conditions in a Treasury decision approved by the President that day. The child adapts the covered tax types, periods, inspecting body, and purpose. C15 uses closely related tax-return inspection machinery but has additional statutory-purpose and effective-date language. C12 shares only generic order phrasing and is a distant third.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"any income, excess profits, declared value excess-profits, capital stock, estate, and gift tax returns for any period to and including 1949 shall be open to inspection by the Special Committee","parent_excerpt":"income, excess-profits, and declared value excess-profits tax returns made under the Internal Revenue Code for the year 1939 and subsequent years shall be open for inspection by the Military Renegotiation Policy and Review Board","explanation":"The central operative clause has the same distinctive subject-and-command construction, with the covered returns, periods, and inspecting body adapted."},{"child_excerpt":"subject to the conditions stated in the Treasury decision relating to the inspection of such returns by that Committee, approved by me this date","parent_excerpt":"subject to the conditions stated in the Treasury decision relating to the inspection of returns by such Board, approved by me this day","explanation":"This is near-verbatim shared administrative machinery tying inspection authority to a contemporaneously approved Treasury decision."}]}
